howto.title: How to play
howto.goal.title: The aim
howto.goal.body:
Flick the striker from your baseline to knock coins into the four corner pockets.
There are {coins} white coins, {coins} black coins and one red coin, the queen.
howto.shoot.title: Taking a shot
howto.shoot.body:
Drag along your baseline to place the striker; it can't sit on top of a coin.
Press the striker, pull back to aim and set the power, and let go. Release near where you pressed to cancel.
Pocketing a coin you are allowed to pocket gives you another shot. The striker never falls into a pocket, so there is no striker foul.
howto.colour.title: Colour game
howto.colour.body:
The side that breaks plays white; the other side plays black. Pocket your own colour.
If you pocket an opponent's coin it stays down for them, and your turn ends unless one of your own went down in the same shot.
The board ends when a side has pocketed all {coins} of its coins. The winner scores 1 point for each coin the other side still has on the board, plus {red} for the queen if the winner covered it.
Once the winner has the target minus {margin} or more, the queen adds nothing. Play one board, or first to 19 or 29 points (at most {boards} boards; the side ahead wins).
howto.point.title: Point game
howto.point.body:
Every coin is fair game for both sides: white {white}, black {black}, queen {queen} (the queen still needs a cover).
The board ends when every coin is down; each side keeps what it pocketed, {perBoard} points in all.
Play one board, or first to 300.
howto.queen.title: The queen and the cover
howto.queen.body:
You may pocket the queen only after your side has pocketed a coin this board. Pocket it earlier and it goes back to the centre.
After the queen, cover it: pocket one of your coins in the same shot or on your very next shot. If you don't, the queen goes back to the centre and the turn passes.
howto.lastCoin.title: The last coin
howto.lastCoin.body:
While the queen is still on the board, a side may not pocket its last coin. In the point game, nobody may pocket the last white or the last black coin.
If it happens, that coin goes back to the centre and the turn passes.
In the colour game, pocketing the opponent's last coin wins the board for them — unless the queen is still on the board, in which case the coin comes back.
howto.turns.title: Turns, teams and the clock
howto.turns.body:
Turns pass to the player on the right. In 2 v 2, partners sit opposite each other.
With the shot clock on, you have {clock} seconds per shot. When time runs out the turn passes; after {timeouts} in a row, a bot plays for that player until they tap "Take back control".
A returned coin goes on the centre spot, or the nearest free place.

ludo.howto.title: How to play Ludo
ludo.howto.goal.title: Goal
ludo.howto.goal.body: Each player has {tokens} tokens in their yard. Race them once around the board, up your own coloured column and into home. The first to bring all {tokens} home wins.
ludo.howto.turn.title: Your turn
ludo.howto.turn.body: The die is rolled for you (or tap it, with "Tap to roll" on). Then tap a glowing token to move it that many squares. If no token can move, the turn passes.
ludo.howto.leave.title: Leaving the yard
ludo.howto.leave.body:
A token leaves the yard only on a {six}, onto your start square.
A {six} gives another roll, but {sixes} sixes in a row lose the turn.
ludo.howto.capture.title: Capturing
ludo.howto.capture.body: Land on an opponent's token to send it back to its yard. A capture gives you another roll.
ludo.howto.safe.title: Safe squares
ludo.howto.safe.body: Start squares and star squares are safe: no token can be captured there.
ludo.howto.home.title: Going home
ludo.howto.home.body: After one lap a token turns into its own column of {column} squares, then home. Reaching home gives another roll.
ludo.howto.presets.title: BD rules and classic
ludo.howto.presets.body:
BD rules (the default): you need the exact roll to reach home, and two of your tokens on one square block others only on a safe square.
Classic: a bigger roll still finishes, and two of your tokens on any square form a block no opponent can pass or land on.
ludo.howto.teams.title: 2 v 2
ludo.howto.teams.body: Partners sit opposite. Partners never capture or block each other. A team wins when both partners have every token home; a partner who finishes first is skipped.
ludo.howto.quick.title: Quick game
ludo.howto.quick.body: The first token home wins (in 2 v 2, one token of each partner).
ludo.howto.clock.title: Clock and bots
ludo.howto.clock.body: Online, each turn has {clock} s. When time runs out your furthest token moves for you; after {timeouts} timeouts in a row a bot plays your seat until you tap "Take back control".

callbreak.howto.title: How to play Callbreak
callbreak.howto.goal.title: Goal
callbreak.howto.goal.body: Four players, each on their own. Every round you call how many tricks you will win, then try to win exactly that many or a few more. The highest total after all rounds wins.
callbreak.howto.deal.title: The deal
callbreak.howto.deal.body: All 52 cards are dealt: {hand} each. The deal moves one seat round the table every round.
callbreak.howto.call.title: The call
callbreak.howto.call.body: Starting left of the dealer, everyone calls {min} to {max}: the tricks they expect to win. Count your sure tricks: high spades, aces, and short suits you can trump.
callbreak.howto.play.title: Playing a trick
callbreak.howto.play.body: The player left of the dealer leads the first trick; the winner of each trick leads the next. You must follow the suit that was led, and if you can beat the best card so far, you must.
callbreak.howto.trumps.title: Spades are trumps
callbreak.howto.trumps.body: Spades beat every other suit. With none of the led suit, you must play a spade that wins the trick if you have one; otherwise play any card. The highest spade, or else the highest card of the led suit, wins.
callbreak.howto.score.title: Scoring
callbreak.howto.score.body:
Win at least your call: you score the call, plus 0.1 for each extra trick (call 4, win 5 = 4.1).
Win fewer: you lose the call (call 4, win 3 = −4).
callbreak.howto.length.title: Game length
callbreak.howto.length.body: A game is {rounds} rounds ({short} for a short game). The highest total wins; equal totals share a place.
callbreak.howto.redeal.title: Redeal
callbreak.howto.redeal.body: With "redeal" on (the default), a hand with no spade and no face card (J, Q, K) is thrown in and all cards are dealt again.
callbreak.howto.clock.title: Clock and bots
callbreak.howto.clock.body: Online, each call or card has {clock} s. When time runs out a move is made for you; after {timeouts} timeouts in a row a bot plays your seat until you tap "Take back control". The host can fill empty seats with bots.

nodi.howto.title: How to play Nodi Par
nodi.howto.demo: Two bots play the opening of a round.
nodi.howto.goal.title: Goal
nodi.howto.goal.body: Moor your boats on the char islands of the river. Hold more islands than the other side, and link your bank to the far bank for a par. Best of {rounds} rounds: {wins} round wins take the match.
nodi.howto.turn.title: Your turn
nodi.howto.turn.body:
Each player has {boats} boats. On your turn, launch a new boat from your bank — slide it along the bank, then drag back and let go, like a carrom striker — or flick one of your boats already on the river.
A round lasts {launches} launches + {flicks} extra flicks each.
nodi.howto.moor.title: Mooring and islands
nodi.howto.moor.body: When everything stops, a boat whose centre is inside an island ring is moored. An island belongs to the side with the most boats moored on it; a tie belongs to nobody. Knock the other side's boats off to take an island back.
nodi.howto.whirl.title: Whirlpools and rocks
nodi.howto.whirl.body: A boat that slides into a whirlpool goes back to its owner's bank (you can launch it again). Rocks are fixed: boats bounce off them.
nodi.howto.par.title: Par
nodi.howto.par.body: A par is a chain of your islands, each next to the last on the river's fixed island map, from your bank to the opposite bank. The chain is drawn across the river in your colour.
nodi.howto.score.title: Scoring
nodi.howto.score.body: At the end of a round: {island} point per island, {centre} for the big centre island, and +{par} for a par. The higher score wins the round.
nodi.howto.borsha.title: Borsha (monsoon) mode
nodi.howto.borsha.body: A steady current flows across the river and pushes moving boats downstream. Boats at rest stay put. Aim upstream!
nodi.howto.teams.title: 2 v 2
nodi.howto.teams.body: Four banks on a cross-shaped river. Partners sit opposite each other and score together; your par links your bank to your partner's.
nodi.howto.clock.title: Turn clock
nodi.howto.clock.body: With the clock on, you have {clock} seconds to move. Run out and that move is lost; after {timeouts} in a row a bot plays for you until you take back control.
